description:
Problem and initialization: The reference program models a customer order for CVRP and evaluates it by constructing routes under configured limits. Its example constructs a nearest-neighbor order before trying several methods, including VNS.

VNS flow: Randomly shake the current order, run local search with swap or insertion, and compare the result with the saved value. A strict improvement updates the best and restarts the neighborhood sequence; otherwise the next neighborhood is tried. The timer can end the search.

Boundary: After an unsuccessful local search, the code keeps the shaken current order but retains the previous current value, so the next iteration is not a standard revert-to-incumbent VNS. The example uses an external data file and imports solver.py before creating its log directory. The CVRP evaluator accepts a finite-cost order with a duplicated customer and a missing customer; validate coverage independently before trusting its feasibility or output.
